milestones.title: Offline-First Frontend
milestones.description: Frontend-first offline operation using Drift/local persistence, local-first reads and writes, an explicit outbox, connectivity state, and simulated synchronization. No real backend integration.

tasks.title: Synchronization domain contracts and state machine
tasks.objective: Represent pending, in-flight, synced, failed, conflict, and rejected local operations with deterministic transitions.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Pure domain entities and transition rules with opaque payloads; conflict policy remains unresolved and no winner is selected.
acceptanceCriteria: All six states round-trip to the documented vocabulary.
Invalid transitions fail loudly.
Retry count and server error are retained.
Conflict and rejection remain explicit.
tests: Unit tests for success, retry, conflict, rejection, invalid transitions, and state serialization.

tasks.title: Durable local outbox persistence
tasks.objective: Persist local operations durably so pending work survives process termination and restart.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Extend the existing Drift repository boundary around the sync queue with state, snapshot, timestamps, retry metadata, and deterministic reads/writes; retain idempotency keys. The M3 SQLite simulation does not claim production encryption at rest: the unspecified platform key-management/encrypted-database decision is documented as DEFERRED_BY_AUTHORITY in docs/M3_SECURITY_DISPOSITION.md.
acceptanceCriteria: A queued operation can be written and read through a repository abstraction.
State, retry count, last error, timestamps, and opaque payload survive reopening the database.
Duplicate idempotency keys are not silently duplicated.
tests: Drift repository round trip, restart persistence, duplicate key, and error metadata tests.

tasks.title: Local-first technician data repositories
tasks.objective: Allow technician screens to read cached data and record local changes without a backend.
tasks.expectedImplementation: LocalDataSource and repository boundaries for the existing M2 technician records: agenda appointments and service-order summaries/details (including customer, location, equipment, status, priority, SLA, and scheduled time). Local writes update the local record and enqueue an operation carrying a separate record type/id association.
acceptanceCriteria: Home, agenda, and orders read assigned/scheduled cached records without a backend.
A supported local mutation updates the local record before any sync attempt.
The mutation is persisted transactionally with an outbox operation containing an entity association, operation type, opaque payload, and sync metadata.
The operation's idempotency key is never used as the business record identity.
The same record can derive its pending/failed/conflict/rejected state from associated operations.
A file-backed database reopen restores cached records and pending operations.
Cached content and a recoverable local error state remain visible.
tests: Repository tests for cached agenda/order reads without a remote source.
Use-case tests for immediate local write and operation-to-record association.
Transaction test proving record update and outbox insertion are atomic.
File-backed restart test proving record, payload, association, retry metadata, and state survive close/reopen.
Record sync-state derivation tests for pending, synced, failed, conflict, and rejected.

tasks.title: Connectivity and simulated synchronization worker
tasks.objective: Simulate reconnect synchronization, retry, deferred work, conflict, and rejection without a remote API.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Application-layer connectivity abstraction with a deterministic simulated source and observable state; a durable worker loads eligible operations in creation order, persists each transition, and accepts injectable synced/failed/conflict/rejected outcomes. Retry uses explicit resend eligibility rather than an invented production schedule.
acceptanceCriteria: Offline operations remain pending and no worker attempt starts.
OFFLINE → ONLINE emits a reconnect event that automatically starts one deterministic worker run.
The worker loads eligible pending/failed operations from the durable repository and persists in-flight before terminal state.
Multiple operations process in deterministic creation order and one operation's terminal state does not corrupt another.
Failures persist retry count and literal error; failed operations become eligible through an explicit retry/resend use case.
No concrete retry timing or maximum is invented; production backoff policy is documented DEFERRED until authoritative/backend policy exists.
Conflict and rejected outcomes remain explicit and never select a winner.
Attachments are represented as independently queued operations that may complete after their parent record.
tests: Deterministic tests for offline, reconnect-triggered automatic synchronization, multiple-operation ordering, failure, resend eligibility, retry, conflict, rejected, and deferred attachment ordering.

tasks.title: Connection band and record synchronization badges
tasks.objective: Expose offline, syncing, pending, synced, failed, conflict, and rejected states in the established design system.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Reusable accessible widgets fed by observable application synchronization state. The connection band derives online/unstable/offline/syncing/pending/all-synced presentation from connectivity and durable operation aggregates; record badges derive only from operations associated with that record.
acceptanceCriteria: The connection band remains visible across all technician tabs while offline, unstable, syncing, or pending work exists.
Pending count and syncing progress are textual and localized.
The all-synced state is shown then self-dismisses according to the documented UX behavior.
Record badges are not color-only and include the documented state labels.
Changing a durable operation state updates its associated record badge without hardcoded counters or UI-only state.
tests: Widget semantics for every connectivity and record state.
Responsive tests across supported window classes.
Provider/state transition tests proving widgets consume repository/application state.
Cross-tab persistence test for the connection band.

tasks.title: Sync Center S01
tasks.objective: Implement the authoritative Sync Center structure for pending operations and explicit recovery states.
tasks.expectedImplementation: S01 route/screen backed only by observable repository/application state, showing operation description, related OS/entity, timestamp, retry count, server error, resend action, and conflict entry point. The UI never mutates Drift directly.
acceptanceCriteria: Pending, syncing, failed, conflict, rejected, and empty/all-synced states are distinguishable using the prototype's hierarchy and labels.
Pending rows are sourced from durable outbox data and update reactively.
Failed rows expose persisted retry count and server error.
Manual resend calls an application use case, makes the operation eligible, and lets the worker persist the next state.
Conflict details preserve both versions, timestamps, impact, and source-defined actions without selecting a winner while OQ-002 remains unresolved.
The screen communicates that pending local data remains protected.
tests: Widget tests for each S01 state and actual repository-backed row contents.
Manual resend interaction test proving no direct database access from presentation.
Accessibility, localization, responsive, and empty/all-synced tests.

tasks.title: Offline lifecycle integration and QA
tasks.objective: Prove the offline-first lifecycle in the independently executable Flutter app.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Compose local persistence, authoritative technician repositories, worker, connection band, record badges, and S01 into app startup and QA flows using a deterministic simulated connectivity/result source only.
acceptanceCriteria: ONLINE → local technician record mutation → durable operation → synced passes.
OFFLINE → local technician record mutation → immediate UI update → pending badge → durable outbox passes.
Close/reinitialize the persistence/application composition and verify the pending operation and record state survive.
Reconnect automatically starts the worker and visibly passes through syncing to a terminal outcome.
Synced, failed/retry, conflict, and rejected terminal paths are inspectable in UI and logs.
Multiple queued operations remain ordered and deterministic.
Evidence artifacts identify each prototype state, Flutter state, screenshot, and conformity result; video remains disabled.
tests: Flutter integration tests with file-backed Drift and composed providers for offline write, restart, reconnect, success, failure/retry, conflict, rejected, and multiple-operation scenarios.
Patrol Android flow using the emulator with screenshots enabled and video disabled.
Prototype ↔ Flutter evidence review for every mapped M3 visual state.
definitionOfDone: Codex conformity pass for each mapped state

milestones.title: Complete Technician Journey
milestones.description: Complete the state-driven technician service-order journey as a backend-independent, local-first frontend while preserving current b1208 contract semantics for M6.

tasks.title: Technician journey domain contracts
tasks.objective: Represent backend-aware OS identity, independent technician stages, allowed primary actions, and invalid-transition rules.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Pure domain journey state/action model preserving backend raw status/code/catalog separately from mobile technician stage.
tasks.offlineBehavior: State changes are local application decisions and produce traceable local operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Primary action derives from current stage and configuration.
Invalid actions are rejected.
Backend status identity is preserved and never replaced by a fixed Flutter enum.
Check-out and finalization remain separate actions.

tasks.title: Offline OS execution persistence
tasks.objective: Persist structured OS execution data and transactional local mutations on top of M3 Drift/outbox infrastructure.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Structured local OS, assignment, customer, service, and execution records through repository/local-data-source boundaries; remove authoritative mock fallback.
tasks.offlineBehavior: Each mutation validates, updates local state, persists atomically, enqueues an associated outbox operation, and returns immediately.
acceptanceCriteria: Cached OS data reads without backend.
Record and outbox commit atomically.
Backend IDs, status identity, nullable values, timestamps, and relationships survive restart.
Local-only sync metadata remains separate.

tasks.title: Travel, maps, check-in, and check-out
tasks.objective: Implement state-driven travel and visit-presence actions with future-compatible waypoint mapping.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Location/maps abstractions, deterministic fixture, travel/check-in/out use cases and local event records.
tasks.offlineBehavior: Travel and presence actions work offline and enqueue durable operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Waypoint preserves OS/technician/type/coordinate/time semantics.
Low precision and out-of-range are explicit.
No invented geofence threshold.
Check-out does not finalize the OS.

tasks.title: Checklist and service execution
tasks.objective: Implement structured checklist responses and service observations using backend-compatible identity and gate semantics.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Separate template, OS association, executable instance, section/item, response, evidence, action-plan, and result concepts.
tasks.offlineBehavior: Autosave each response and service-data mutation locally with durable outbox association.
acceptanceCriteria: Response type/value/required/NA/conformity semantics are preserved.
Conditional and reproved-item behavior is configuration-driven.
Reproved items require authoritative evidence/action-plan data.
Progress survives restart.
evidence: O10 progress, conditional, reproved, and evidence captures

tasks.title: Parts and service data
tasks.objective: Represent product, OS part request/usage, stock/reservation, and shipment as distinct concepts.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Separate local product/catalog, request/usage, stock/reservation, and shipment representations with explicit mapping classifications.
tasks.offlineBehavior: Supported part actions update local state and enqueue operations without direct stock mutation.
acceptanceCriteria: OS/product/request identifiers are preserved.
Quantity requested/released/applied semantics remain distinct.
Lot/serial are only represented where authoritative evidence supports them.
Shipment is not collapsed into OS part usage.

tasks.title: Photos, attachments, and signature
tasks.objective: Capture local evidence and signature data with backend-compatible metadata and independent attachment synchronization.
tasks.expectedImplementation: App-private local files plus explicit attachment/evidence/signature metadata, capture, clear/redo, acceptance, and outbox operations.
tasks.offlineBehavior: Capture works offline; metadata and local file survive restart; attachments may sync after parent record.
acceptanceCriteria: OS photos and checklist evidence remain distinct mappings.
Signature includes acceptance statement and supports clear/redo.
Local paths and sync metadata remain local-only.
Video/resumable upload remains deferred when unspecified.
definitionOfDone: No universal backend attachment DTO invented

tasks.title: Completion review and finalization
tasks.objective: Implement named completion blockers and separate check-out from configured OS finalization.
tasks.expectedImplementation: Application completion use case coordinating configured checklist, signature, parts, check-out, and status gates.
tasks.offlineBehavior: Ready completion is recorded locally and queued as a durable operation.
acceptanceCriteria: Each blocker is named with a shortcut.
Finalization does not invent required fields.
Check-out remains separate from finalization.
Offline completion survives restart and exposes pending synchronization.
evidence: O18 blocked, ready, and completed captures

tasks.title: Complete journey QA and conformity
tasks.objective: Prove the complete technician journey, M3 synchronization integration, backend traceability, and prototype conformity.
tasks.expectedImplementation: End-to-end composed lifecycle and evidence package; no second sync engine and no real backend.
tasks.offlineBehavior: Prove local mutation, restart, pending, reconnect, syncing, synced, failed/retry, conflict, rejected, multiple operations, and pending attachment.
acceptanceCriteria: Every domain/repository/outbox contract is classified DIRECT, SMALL_ADAPTER, MATERIAL_ADAPTER, BACKEND_GAP, or DEFERRED_TO_M6.
Every mapped prototype state has paired Chrome/CDP and Flutter/Patrol evidence.
REQ-SEC-003 remains DEFERRED_BY_AUTHORITY.
tests: Patrol Android with screenshots enabled and video disabled
